newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to tighten mining rules after Busang.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to tighten mining rules after Busang.

text.p: Indonesian Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Tuesday the government will tighten mining regulations following the Busang scandal.

He also told a news conference the government was considering requiring foreign mining companies to allocate at least a 10-percent stake in their projects to the government under the next batch of contracts of work (COW) to be awarded.
"We will tighten mining regulations because there are holes (in existing rules) that are being made use of by people," Sudjana said. "We will cover these areas in future contracts."

Consultant Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd has said geological samples from the Busang gold field -- touted by Bre-X Minerals Ltd as the find of the century -- had been falsified on a scale "without precedent in the history of mining anywhere in the world".
